Each node is shaded by the size of the largest clique containing it: A, B and C are in the triangle, size 3, and D only in the edge, size 2, as the table lists." width="100%"} For every node, the number of nodes in the largest maximal clique it belongs to. It measures how embedded a node is in a tightly knit group: a node in a large clique sits in a dense core (a close team, a protein complex), while a node whose largest clique is an edge has no triangles at all. The maximum over all nodes is the clique number (see `clique_number()`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of nodes (IDs or labels) to report. If `None` (default), all nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID to the size of its largest clique (`1` for an isolated node). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Computed from the maximal cliques of `find_cliques()` (Bron-Kerbosch), as in NetworkX's `node_clique_number`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0c90ba0a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")]) {g.get_label_from_id(n): k for n, k in g.node_clique_number().items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 3, 'B': 3, 'C': 3, 'D': 2} ``` ::: :::
